ECCC-SPS-fea1-1496.title: Special weather statement
ECCC-SPS-fea1-1496.text: A significant Fall storm will impact northern Manitoba beginning Friday evening and will persist through the weekend. The precipitation with this storm will begin as rain for most communities then transition to heavy, wet snow. Current forecast guidance suggests total snowfall amounts of 15 to 25 cm are possible, with the highest snowfall accumulations over Brochet and Tadoule Lake. Rainfall totals are forecast to be in the range of 20 to 40 mm. Strong winds are also forecast, with wind gusts possibly up to 90 km/h. Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow are expected when these winds combine with falling snow. Freezing rain is also likely with this storm, specifically for Lynn Lake, Tadoule Lake, and Brochet. Conditions will improve on Sunday as the snow tapers off and winds diminish. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media u

ECCC-SPS-fea1-1855.region: Buffalo Narrows and Peter Pond Lake
ECCC-SPS-fea1-1855.title: Special weather statement
ECCC-SPS-fea1-1855.text: A significant fall storm will impact northern Saskatchewan beginning on Friday and will persist through Saturday. The precipitation with this storm will begin as rain before transitioning over to heavy, wet snow. Current guidance suggests that the highest snowfall accumulations will likely be for the regions of Cree Lake - Key Lake, Uranium City - Camsell Portage, Fond-du-Lac - Stony Rapids, and Wollaston Lake - Collins Bay, where total amounts of 25 to 50 cm are possible. Strong winds are also expected with this storm on Saturday, with wind gusts of 60 to 80 km/h possible. Reduced visibility in blowing snow may occur when these winds combine with the falling snow. For southern and eastern regions the rain may not change to snow until Saturday. For these regions, total rainfall amounts of 20 to 40 mm is possible. Conditions will improve Saturday night and Sunday as the snow tapers off and winds diminish. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To r

ECCC-SPS-fea1-861.title: Special weather statement
ECCC-SPS-fea1-861.text: The first notable accumulating snowfall of the season is expected, primarily over higher terrain. Locations: south coast of Newfoundland from Burgeo to the Burin Peninsula as well as Clarenville and vicinity. Potential snowfall: 2 to 5 cm, highest over higher terrain. Time span: Friday morning to Friday afternoon. Remarks: As temperatures hover near the freezing mark, snowfall accumulations may vary over short distances. Precipitation should remain primarily as rain over lower elevations along the coast. Be prepared for winter driving conditions, particularly over higher terrain sections of the Bay d'Espoir Highway, Burin Peninsula Highway, Burgeo Highway, and the Trans-Canada Highway between Goobies and Port Blandford. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

ECCC-FTA-fea1-1269.title: Frost advisory
ECCC-FTA-fea1-1269.text: Patchy frost is possible overnight into Friday morning, particularly for areas well inland from Lake Ontario. Take preventative measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees, and crops. Cover up plants, especially those in frost-prone areas. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

ECCC-WDW-fea1-854.title: Wind warning
ECCC-WDW-fea1-854.text: Strong winds are expected. Locations: south coast of Newfoundland from Burgeo to the Burin Peninsula, and the southern Avalon Peninsula. Maximum wind gusts: northeasterly 80 km/h, except 100 along parts of the coast. Time span: Friday afternoon and evening. Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

ECCC-WDW-fea1-858.title: Wind warning
ECCC-WDW-fea1-858.text: Strong winds are expected. Locations: south coast of Newfoundland from Burgeo to the Burin Peninsula, and the southern Avalon Peninsula. Maximum wind gusts: northeasterly 80 km/h, except 100 along parts of the coast. Time span: Friday afternoon and evening. Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

ECCC-WDW-fea1-2534.title: Wind warning
ECCC-WDW-fea1-2534.text: Damaging winds are expected. Strong easterly winds, with gusts to 90 km/h at times, are expected tonight. There may be blowing snow at times with these strong winds. Winds will diminish Friday morning. Some property damage is possible. Secure loose objects. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

ECCC-WDW-fea1-2532.title: Wind warning
ECCC-WDW-fea1-2532.text: Damaging winds are occurring. Sustained winds of 70 km/h, with gusts up to 90 km/h, will continue into the evening and slowly diminish through the night. Some property damage is possible. If outside, protect yourself from flying or falling debris. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

ECCC-RFW-fea1-801.title: Rainfall warning
ECCC-RFW-fea1-801.text: Very heavy rain is expected. Locations: Guysborough County, Richmond County, Sydney Metro and Cape Breton County. Total rainfall: 50 to 70 mm. Time span: continuing tonight and Friday. Remarks: Gusty winds accompanying the rain may cause tree branches to break. Local utility outages are possible. Rainfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to rainfall amounts. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NSstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NSStorm.

ECCC-BZW-fea1-2532.title: Blizzard warning
ECCC-BZW-fea1-2532.text: Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in snow and blowing snow continue. Blizzard conditions will persist until the overnight hours. Visibility will slowly improve Friday morning. Travel will likely be hazardous. Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.
